source: Tribal Lands Ceded to the United States (georeferenced Royce cession maps)
publisher: USDA Forest Service (Office of Tribal Relations; Geospatial Service and Technology Center)
content: 718 polygons from 67 Royce maps; cessions and reservations 1784-1894; up to 5 dates per cession; links to Kappler texts, statutes, executive orders; present-day tribes/states/counties
format: ArcGIS REST (JSON/GeoJSON/PBF), GeoJSON, Shapefile ZIP, CSV, KML
license_or_terms: CC BY 4.0 per both Data.gov listings (tribal-lands-ceded-to-the-united-states-feature-layer and ...-cf3ca; issued 2017-04-12, modified 2022-08-29); agency metadata XML (S_USA.TRIBALCEDEDLANDS.xml, metadata date 2018-05-29) gives Use constraints "This data is for informational purposes only.", Access constraints "None", and no license text; credit "USDA Forest Service Office of Tribal Relations"; no Forest Service Research Data Archive record found
update_status: First published 2017-04-12; last updated 2022-08-29; updates none planned
notes: Core backbone for time slider. 7 cession IDs (47,65,128,129,130,543,690) lack geometry. Counts disagree (718 vs 752 polygons; 1172 table rows). Overlaps likely; do not sum acreage. Contact USFS Office of Tribal Relations to confirm license.

source: Indian Land Cessions in the United States (Royce, 1899) - original maps and schedule
publisher: Library of Congress (Law Library); originally Smithsonian Bureau of American Ethnology 18th Annual Report
content: 67 maps and 2 tables compiled by Charles C. Royce; Schedule of Indian Land Cessions
format: Image, PDF, online text, IIIF manifest
license_or_terms: Public domain per Library of Congress
notes: Source of record for GEO-001. Reflects 1890s federal view of cessions; not Indigenous territory. Classifies by legal type (treaty, unratified, executive order).

source: Invasion of America (interactive map)
publisher: Claudio Saunt (University of Georgia); hosted at invasionofamerica.ehistory.org
content: Time-lapse of transfer of Indian land 1776-1887 built on Royce data
license_or_terms: No download or license found; site fetch blocked by robots
notes: Task brief attributed this to University of Richmond DSL; sources read credit Saunt/UGA and show no Richmond link (unconfirmed). Saunt is credited on the USFS dataset.

source: Morrill Act of 1862 Indigenous Land Parcels Database (Land-Grab U)
publisher: High Country News (Robert Lee); hosted on GitHub
content: 162 cession polygons, about 79,461 parcels, universities; built on Royce maps plus supplementary maps
license_or_terms: Conflict confirmed: repo LICENSE file text is CC0 1.0 Universal (and the sidebar says CC0-1.0); README and landgrabu.org say the database is under the Open Database License and contents under CC BY-SA (README links CC BY-SA 3.0); the hcn.org/issues/land-grab-universities page states no data license (its article text is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) and only links the repo; cite as Robert Lee, "Morrill Act of 1862 Indigenous Land Parcels Database", High Country News, March 2020. Ask landgrabu@hcn.org which governs.
notes: Case-study layer, not base layer. Share-alike obligations. Contact landgrabu@hcn.org. No tribal consultation described.

format: Web portal (no API or download documented)
license_or_terms: Not stated; described as free public resource; disclaimer page not read
update_status: Phased expansion; phase 4 under way as of Nov 2023
notes: Link target and citation aid. Ask OSU (lib-dls@okstate.edu) before bulk reuse.

source: Atlas of Historical County Boundaries

notes: Gives jurisdictional context by year; does not map Indigenous nations. Use state/territory files for slider; counties on demand.

source: Native Land Digital API (territories, languages, treaties)
publisher: Native Land Digital (Indigenous-led nonprofit, Canada)
content: Global polygons: Indigenous territories, languages, treaties; point-in-polygon queries; full GeoJSON dumps
format: GeoJSON; GET/POST JSON API (native-land.ca/api/index.php); iframe embed
license_or_terms: Three sources disagree. (1) Indigenous Data Sovereignty Treaty (api-docs.native-land.ca/data-sovereignty-treaty): permitted = educational/research aligned with IDS, non-commercial applications that generate no revenue, Indigenous-led initiatives; prohibited = charging for access or integration, commercial use, modifying boundaries without consultation and approval, misrepresenting territories, derivatives that do not acknowledge Indigenous ownership, storing or distributing API data without explicit NLD permission; attribution to NLD and acknowledgement of Indigenous communities required; NLD may revoke access and take legal action. (2) api-docs About-and-disclaimers: "not under any proprietary license; the work can be considered under a CC0 license", yet "not meant or reasonably to use for academic or legal purposes". (3) native-land.ca FAQ: commercial use "No", suggested credit "Used with permission for educational and non-commercial purposes", maps "should not be used for legal claims, land disputes"; site footer "©Native Land Digital 2024, All rights reserved." API key (required since late 2024) requires ticking an agreement box. No document is titled Terms of Use; no way to request permission is stated. Not legal advice.
notes: Ask NLD for written permission before any proxy or snapshot. CORS unverified. Key cannot be secret in client code. Disclaimer: not official or legal boundaries.

notes: Scope and US coverage unclear; no documented treaty-date field; Cession numbering resembles Royce but unconfirmed.
